# Generated files: what churns and what to do

| File class | Symptom | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| TMP font atlas (Dynamic font asset) | edited in 80+ commits | build static atlases once; keep dynamic ones out of feature commits; commit atlas refreshes alone |
| `link.xml`, Addressables settings | edited by tools on every build | commit in their own "build config" commits |
| Solution/project files (`*.sln`, `*.slnx`, `*.csproj`) | tracked by accident | ignore |
| Localization tables / csv exports | nine tables change together | regenerate from the csv source of truth in a dedicated commit |
| Graph/index tool output (code graph, caches) | thousands of tracked files, imported by Unity | write outside `Assets/`, ignore, `git rm --cached` |
| Editor screenshot hotkeys | `Assets/2026-..png` in the repo | save outside `Assets/` or ignore the pattern |
| Build reports / memory captures / recordings | local output | ignore |
| `packages-lock.json` | changes with every package edit | tracked on purpose (reproducible git packages); commit with the manifest change |
| `ProjectSettings` | big diffs from small toggles | review the diff; keep unrelated toggles out of feature commits |
| Mesh/asset bakes | huge text YAML | binary or FBX, generated by an idempotent tool, header in the generator |

Rules
- A generated file must be reproducible from a tool in the repo; if it is not, treat it as source and review it.
- Header in generated code: `// GENERATED by <tool>, do not edit`.
- After adding an ignore rule run `git check-ignore -v` on a first-party file to prove the rule does not swallow it; then clone fresh and compile.
- Large generated data is never stored as YAML text.
